new_text.oculon_dossier: Dossier on a company, person or project: Wikipedia profile and readership spike, Hacker News stories, news, related Polymarket markets, new GitHub repos, SEC filings (if enabled), merged into one timeline with a fused signal.
new_text.oculon_email_security: Can someone send email that looks like it comes from this domain? Checks SPF, DMARC, DKIM, MTA-STS, TLS reporting, BIMI, CAA and DNSSEC from public DNS, and returns a verdict (spoofable, partly protected, protected), a 0-100 score and the fixes in order.
new_text.oculon_entity: Look up an entity in the Oculon graph and its neighbors. Ids look like "domain:openai.com", "org:nvidia", "aircraft:a835af", "company:falcon landing llc".
new_text.oculon_exposure: A domain's internet exposure: resolves its main hosts and known subdomains, then lists open ports, software and known CVEs per IP from Shodan InternetDB (free). CDN edges are marked.
new_text.oculon_fact_check: Fact check a claim, or the main claim of a news link. Finds published fact checks (Google Fact Check Tools: Snopes, AFP, PolitiFact, Full Fact and others) and current reporting, then gives a verdict (true, mostly true, mixed, misleading, false, unverified) with a confidence and a summary that cites
new_text.oculon_feedback_stats: Useful/Noise votes per module and how far each module alert bar has moved because of them.
new_text.oculon_fence_check: Check every geofence now and report what is new inside each since the previous check.
new_text.oculon_fence_list: List geofences with their boxes and what each watches.
new_text.oculon_fires: Active fires and thermal hotspots near a place in the last 1-5 days from NASA FIRMS (VIIRS satellites): clusters with detection count and fire radiative power. Catches wildfires, industrial fires and strikes on infrastructure.
new_text.oculon_footprint: Pre-release footprints of a domain: hostnames that newly appeared in Certificate Transparency logs, pages newly archived by the Wayback Machine, and newly created public GitHub repos. Good for spotting unannounced products.
new_text.oculon_hazards: Official orange and red disaster alerts from GDACS (UN/EU): earthquakes, cyclones, floods, volcanoes, droughts, wildfires, with severity and countries, plus tsunami bulletins and extreme US weather alerts.
new_text.oculon_health: Company early-warning score 0-100 from hiring momentum, new federal lawsuits, insider selling, news tone, GitHub shipping and the stock move, with every component explained and a 30-day history.
new_text.oculon_hype: Hype-cycle phase of a topic (DORMANT, EMERGING, RISING, PEAK, COOLING, STEADY) from 8 weeks of Wikipedia readers, Hacker News stories, global news share (GDELT), arXiv papers and new GitHub repos.
new_text.oculon_impact: People exposed to current M6+ earthquakes and severe storms (Wikidata settlement populations within the affected radius, plus night-light change when enough nights have passed). Give a place to estimate exposure around it instead.
new_text.oculon_launches: Launch radar for a company: new Hugging Face models/datasets/Spaces, new iOS apps and app updates, new npm packages under its scope, and (with a domain) new hostnames, pages and repos.
new_text.oculon_listen: Transcribe a public audio or video FILE URL (mp3, mp4, wav...; not a YouTube page) with Deepgram and return a machine summary, topics and timestamped passages that mention the subject.
new_text.oculon_markets_crosscheck: Cross-check Polymarket against Kalshi and Manifold: an LLM confirms which markets ask exactly the same question, then gaps between venues are listed. A big gap means one crowd is wrong or knows something first.
new_text.oculon_military_air: Worldwide military air traffic from open ADS-B data, grouped by region, with notable roles (tanker, AWACS, ISR, bomber, maritime patrol) and surges versus the region history.
new_text.oculon_monitor: Create a monitor from a plain-language request, e.g. "tell me when there is an internet outage in Iran", "watch critical CVEs for nginx", "earthquakes above 6 near Tokyo", "news about OpenAI", "travel risk changes for Bangkok". It becomes a watch rule that is re-checked on a schedule and reports onl
new_text.oculon_narratives: News narratives tracked across days (storylines such as a company crisis or an IPO), with stories per day and phase. Set run=true to first group the latest headlines.
new_text.oculon_natural_events: Open natural events from NASA EONET (tropical cyclones, wildfires, volcanoes, floods, icebergs) with a severity score.
new_text.oculon_night_lights: Night-time lights of a place from NASA VIIRS satellite data: recent nights versus a baseline month. A sharp drop can indicate blackout, conflict or evacuation; a rise can indicate new activity.
new_text.oculon_package_vulns: Known vulnerabilities of a software package (OSV.dev), optionally for one version, flagged when exploited in the wild.
new_text.oculon_papers: Research brief on a topic: the most cited papers of recent years, the newest relevant ones, papers per year (is the field growing?), PubMed counts for medical topics, and a short overview that cites the numbered papers. Sources: OpenAlex, PubMed, Semantic Scholar.
new_text.oculon_podcast: Find recent podcast episodes about a subject and transcribe the newest English one (Deepgram, paid per minute with a daily budget): machine summary, topics, and timestamped passages that mention the subject.
new_text.oculon_radar: Global anomaly radar. Finds what the world is suddenly paying attention to right now (Wikipedia readership spikes, Hacker News traction, Polymarket swings, strong earthquakes, severe natural events) and fuses items about the same subject into corroborated signals with evidence.
new_text.oculon_read_page: Fetch a web page and return its readable text (Jina Reader, Firecrawl fallback), capped at about 6000 characters.
new_text.oculon_recall: Is this car or product recalled? Pass a 17-character VIN, "year make model" (e.g. "2018 Honda Accord"), or a product name ("stroller", "peanut butter"). Vehicles: NHTSA safety recalls with do-not-drive and park-outside warnings. Products: CPSC consumer recalls and FDA food, drug and device enforceme
new_text.oculon_regs: US Federal Register: executive orders, final and proposed rules, notices and tomorrow's documents on public inspection, with effective dates and comment deadlines. Filter by text and agency.
new_text.oculon_rewind: Time machine: what Oculon would have seen on a past date. Wikipedia spikes measured against the weeks before, top Hacker News stories, strong earthquakes and that day's Guardian headlines, fused across sources.
new_text.oculon_sanctions: Screen against the US OFAC sanctions (SDN) list: a wallet address (also checks whether it transacted directly with a listed address), a vessel IMO number, or the exact name of a company, person or vessel. Returns SANCTIONED, EXPOSED or CLEAR.
new_text.oculon_satellite_image: True-color satellite image (NASA MODIS, about 250 m) of a place for a date. Returns the image.
new_text.oculon_scam_check: Is this message a scam? Paste an SMS, email or chat message. Every link is checked (Safe Browsing, URLhaus, urlscan.io, domain age, look-alikes), the sender domain is compared with any brand it mentions, and known scam patterns are matched (parcel fees, account locked, one-time codes, gift cards or
new_text.oculon_scoreboard: Forecast track record: counts, Brier scores of the model and of the market, and skill versus the market.
new_text.oculon_sec_events: A company's recent 8-K events decoded into plain English: material agreements, cybersecurity incidents, restructuring, restatements, CEO/CFO departures, bankruptcy.
new_text.oculon_sec_search: SEC EDGAR full-text search across filings since 2001: which companies wrote a phrase (e.g. "cybersecurity incident", "going concern") in a window, with form, date and 8-K items.
new_text.oculon_sentinel_image: Sharp satellite image (Copernicus Sentinel-2, 10 m per pixel; or Sentinel-1 radar that sees through clouds) of a place, least cloudy pass in the window ending on the date. Returns the image.
new_text.oculon_ship: Follow one ship by its 9-digit MMSI and return its latest AIS position, speed and status if it reports within the window.
new_text.oculon_ships: Live vessels around a port or sea area from AIS (aisstream.io), listening for a number of seconds: totals, moving vs anchored/moored, vessel types (cargo, tanker, military...), names. Coverage depends on community receivers; an empty result says so.
new_text.oculon_signals: Most recent signals produced by any Oculon module, with scores and evidence.
new_text.oculon_social_pulse: What people are posting about a subject right now on X, Reddit, TikTok (paid Apify, small daily budget) and Bluesky: post counts per platform, pace over the last day when measurable, most engaged and latest posts with links.
new_text.oculon_space_weather: Current space weather from NOAA SWPC: planetary K index, geomagnetic storm level (G1-G5) and the strongest solar flare of the last 7 days.
new_text.oculon_squawks: Aircraft squawking emergency transponder codes right now (adsb.lol): 7500 hijack, 7600 radio failure, 7700 general emergency, with position, registration and nearest airport.
new_text.oculon_travel: Travel and place risk brief for the coming week: US State Department and UK FCDO advice, 7-day weather warnings (storms, heavy rain, gusts, heat, cold, UV), PM2.5 air quality, WHO disease outbreak news, GDACS disaster alerts, nearby earthquakes, satellite heat detections and confirmed internet outag
new_text.oculon_url_check: Is a link dangerous? Checks Google Safe Browsing, URLhaus (abuse.ch), urlscan.io scan history, domain age and registrar (RDAP), and warning signs in the URL itself (brand names on other domains, punycode, risky TLDs). Returns a verdict (malicious, suspicious, no known threats), a 0-100 risk and the
new_text.oculon_verify_proof: Verify a forecast proof: recompute its hash, check the Merkle path, and check the Bitcoin attestation against the block merkle root. Returns VERIFIED, PENDING, NOT_STAMPED, TAMPERED or ERROR.
new_text.oculon_vessel: Vessel identity from a name, MMSI or IMO (Global Fishing Watch registry data): flag history, type, owners, earlier names, first and last AIS transmission, OFAC sanctions check on the IMO.
new_text.oculon_vulns: Vulnerabilities newly exploited in the wild (CISA KEV) with EPSS odds and due dates, new critical CVEs (NVD) and critical package advisories (GitHub), optionally for one vendor.
new_text.oculon_watch_list: List the watchlist: targets Oculon re-checks for changes (companies, domains, wallets, tokens, planes, topics, night lights, air quality).
new_text.oculon_web_search: Search the web (Tavily, Exa fallback). Returns titles, URLs, snippets and dates.
new_text.oculon_address_check: Check a crypto address before sending funds, without API keys: chain from the address format (Bitcoin, EVM, Solana, Tron), US OFAC sanctions, and balance, transaction count and labels from free explorers (mempool.space, Blockscout, Solana RPC). Flags unused addresses and contracts posing as wallets.
new_text.oculon_breaches: Data breaches from Have I Been Pwned: leave domain empty for the newest breaches, or pass a domain or company name for all of its breaches, with date, accounts affected and the kinds of data exposed.
new_text.oculon_company_lookup: Is this company or supplier real? Pass an EU VAT number (checked live in the European Commission VIES service: valid or not, registered name and address), a 20-character LEI, or a company name (Global LEI Index: legal name, registered address, status, registration number, ultimate parent). Useful be
new_text.oculon_defi: DeFi risk radar (DefiLlama, alternative.me): protocol TVL crashes, stablecoin depegs and supply shocks, recent hacks, chain TVL moves, DEX volume and fee spikes, yield anomalies, crypto fear and greed.
new_text.oculon_doc_check: Was this invoice, bank statement or payment screenshot edited? Reads a PDF, JPEG or PNG: the programs that made and saved it (online PDF editors, image editors), creation vs modification date, how many times it was saved, fonts embedded twice, white boxes over text, annotations, dangerous parts (Jav
new_text.oculon_email_headers: Analyze the raw headers of a suspicious email: SPF, DKIM and DMARC results recorded by the receiving server, the Received path, the origin IP and its country, and spoofing signs (From differs from the envelope sender, Reply-To elsewhere, a display name posing as an address). Returns a verdict and ri
new_text.oculon_hash_check: Is this file known malware, a known good file, or unknown? Pass an MD5, SHA-1 or SHA-256 hash. Checks CIRCL hashlookup (NIST NSRL and other known-software sets), MalwareBazaar, ThreatFox, AlienVault OTX and VirusTotal, and returns a verdict, the malware family when known, the reasons and what to do.
new_text.oculon_honeypot_check: Can this token be sold? Simulates a buy and a sell on the token's main pool and replays recent holders' sells (honeypot.is): honeypot verdict, buy and sell tax, holders who could not sell, unpublished or upgradeable contracts. Chains: eth, bsc, base.
new_text.oculon_iban_check: Check an IBAN before paying an invoice, fully offline: country, length, ISO 13616 mod-97 check digits and the bank code. Pass the supplier country to flag an account held in another country, a common sign of invoice fraud. A valid IBAN does not prove who owns the account.
new_text.oculon_ip_check: Who runs this IP address, and is it known for abuse? Pass an IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a domain (its first address is checked). Returns network (ASN, owner, type), location, flags (Tor exit, proxy, hosting, internet scanner, known benign service), AbuseIPDB reports, GreyNoise scanner status, AlienVau
new_text.oculon_lookalike_domains: Find lookalike domains of a brand that a phisher could use: typos, swapped letters, homoglyphs, extra words and other endings that exist in DNS (with mail servers), plus certificates issued in the last 90 days for any name containing the brand (Certificate Transparency).
new_text.oculon_phone_check: Who is behind this phone number? Pass it in international format (+44 20 7946 0958), or a national number with country. Returns country, line type (mobile, landline, VoIP, premium rate), carrier and location when known, and warnings for premium-rate numbers, UK 070 personal numbers and the Caribbean
new_text.oculon_protocol: One DeFi protocol in depth: TVL per chain, 1d-1y change, drawdown from its high, audits, oracles, hack history, funding rounds and DefiLlama warnings.
new_text.oculon_ransomware: Ransomware leak-site claims collected by ransomware.live. Leave query empty for the newest claims, or pass a two-letter country code ("DE"), a sector ("Healthcare", "Manufacturing") or a company name or domain. Returns victims with group, country, sector and dates, plus counts by group, country and
new_text.oculon_replay: Replay log of an earlier check by its check id: the verdict, what changed since the check before it, and every source called in order with status and time.
new_text.oculon_robinhood: Robinhood Chain (id 4663) right now: chain activity, trending pools and pools created in the last hours, each with risk flags (thin liquidity, buys without sells, sudden dumps).
new_text.oculon_robinhood_deployer: Robinhood Chain deployer reputation: from a token or deployer address, find every token that wallet launched (directly or through a launchpad) and how many are dead now. Flags serial launchers.
new_text.oculon_robinhood_token: Risk read on a Robinhood Chain token: contract verification, top-10 holder concentration, holders, and pool behavior. Returns DANGER, CAUTION, OK or UNKNOWN with reasons.
new_text.oculon_satellites: Satellites from CelesTrak. Leave query empty for everything launched in the last 30 days, grouped by launch. Or pass a satellite name ("ISS", "starlink-1007") or NORAD catalog number for its orbit (perigee, apogee, period, inclination, regime), owner, launch date and status.
new_text.oculon_status: Which Oculon sources are up, slow, degraded or down, from real calls in the last hours: success rate, median time, last error, and sources being skipped (a mirror or cached data answers instead).
new_text.oculon_token: Token contract check: honeypot and owner-power flags, buy/sell tax and holders (GoPlus), DEX pairs and liquidity (DexScreener), price and market cap (CoinGecko). Returns DANGER, CAUTION, OK or UNKNOWN with reasons.
new_text.oculon_wallet: On-chain wallet intelligence for an EVM (0x...) or Solana address: portfolio value and top holdings, first transaction and age, recent transactions, risk labels (GoPlus, Webacy), and balance on Robinhood Chain.

new_text.add_users_to_flag: Change who receives a flag by targeting site user IDs or emails. Append adds a rule; replace removes all existing rules. Preview first, then apply with confirmed=true after user approval.
new_text.capabilities: List the get_data query types by category, with date presets and a schema summary. Filter by category or contains, with detail='full', for a type's filters, output fields, orderBy columns and time units.
new_text.check_tracking: Check whether a website's tracking is installed and receiving page views or has stopped, with blocked-request issues, their fix, and the latest coding-agent install report. Use when data looks missing or after installing.
new_text.create_annotation: Create a chart annotation. confirmed=false (default) returns a preview without writing; confirmed=true creates it.
new_text.create_flag: Create a feature flag, inactive and boolean unless configured. confirmed=false (default) returns a preview without writing; confirmed=true creates it.
new_text.create_funnel: Create a funnel for a website. confirmed=false (default) returns a preview without writing; confirmed=true creates it.
new_text.create_goal: Create a conversion goal. confirmed=false (default) returns a preview without writing; confirmed=true creates it.
new_text.create_link: Create a short link in the website's organization. confirmed=false (default) returns a preview without writing; confirmed=true creates it.
new_text.delete_annotation: Delete a chart annotation people added (source databuddy) from dashboard charts, including public charts if shared; GitHub markers are read-only. Applying marks it deleted; no restore tool is exposed. Preview returns the annotation.
new_text.delete_flag: Archive a feature flag so SDKs stop serving it. Preview returns the flag and any flags that depend on it; apply with confirmed=true after user approval. No restore tool is exposed.
new_text.delete_funnel: Delete a saved funnel. Applying deactivates it and hides it from lists and analytics reads. Preview returns the funnel; no restore tool is exposed.
new_text.delete_goal: Delete a saved conversion goal. Applying deactivates it and hides its definition from lists and analytics reads. Preview returns the goal; no restore tool is exposed.
new_text.delete_link: Delete a short link. confirmed=false (default) returns the link without deleting it; confirmed=true deletes it.
new_text.dismiss_investigation: Close an open investigation with the team's reason, only when the user asks. Future investigations read the note. expected, wrong and not_useful keep the subject quiet for 30 days unless it gets materially worse. Preview returns the case and what closing it does; apply with confirmed=true after user
new_text.execute_sql_query: Run read-only ClickHouse SQL on selected websites in one organization. Use get_schema for table notes and include the website column to break results down by site. If you hit the organization limit, try again in a minute.
new_text.get_account: Return one customer account: its traits and billing, activity for a period, the identified users active in it, its health and the account reviewer's last review. Keys come from list_accounts.
new_text.get_business_context: Return the organization's saved business context: what it does, what its events mean, team priorities, success definitions and measurement plans. Read it before judging conversions, activation or success.
new_text.get_conversion_attribution: Break a goal, funnel or custom event's conversions down by each visitor's first visit: referrer, UTM source/medium/campaign and landing page. touchWebsiteIds adds visits on other websites in the organization.
new_text.get_data: Query website analytics: traffic, pages, referrers and UTM campaigns, devices, countries, errors, Web Vitals, sessions, users, custom events, revenue, uptime and AI traffic. Pass a query type from capabilities, or up to 10 as queries; compare adds the previous period. For joins or custom grouping, u
new_text.get_experiment_results: Return exposed/converted visitors and comparisons per flag arm for visitors the random split assigned since the split last changed (assignmentChangedAt). Fisher when any expected cell is below 5, else a two-proportion z-test; significance uses Holm-adjusted p-values and minimumVisitorsPerArm. Boolea
new_text.get_funnel_analytics: Return per-step conversion and drop-off for one funnel, by funnelId from list_funnels. Visitors entering in range get conversionWindowHours to finish, even past range end. time_series holds at most the latest 90 points. cohort narrows to matching visitors, and breakdown splits by one current profile
new_text.get_funnel_analytics_by_referrer: Return one funnel's conversion broken down by referrer, by funnelId from list_funnels. Paginated over referrers. Referrers with a single visitor are omitted, so totals can be lower than get_funnel_analytics.
new_text.get_goal_analytics: Return entered and completed counts and the conversion rate for one goal, by goalId from list_goals. cohort narrows to matching visitors, and breakdown splits by one current profile trait (top 1-20 values by entrants). Trait filters and breakdowns need read access to the website.
new_text.get_link_analytics: Return click analytics for one short link by ID from list_links or search_links: total clicks, clicks by day, and top referrers, countries and devices for a date range.
new_text.get_log_connection: Check a log connection, such as Axiom, with its provider: the datasets its token reads, each website's links and their problems, and suggested links worked out from what each dataset holds, with the evidence. connectionId from list_integrations.
new_text.get_schema: Return the analytics tables execute_sql_query can read, with column types and the counting rules for each table.
new_text.get_search_console: Google search data for a website from Search Console, read with your own Google account: clicks, impressions, CTR and average position in total and by query, page, country and device, each row with previous for the same-length period just before. page lists the searches that led to one page; query l
new_text.list_accounts: Find customer accounts (groups such as workspaces or companies) with plan, billing status, MRR and activity for a period. Pass needsAttention: true for the accounts the team should act on, with why and what to do. Pass search with a company name or domain to find one account, active or not. Use get_
new_text.list_annotations: List a website's chart annotations, newest first, with their source: databuddy when people added them, or read-only GitHub markers (github_deployment, github_release) for successful production deploys and published releases, with links. github says how far markers reach. from, to and sources narrow
new_text.list_changes: List metric changes Databuddy detected in the last two days for an organization or website, critical and largest first. Changes already open as investigations are left out; list_investigations has those.
new_text.list_flags: List feature flags with their status, rollout, rules, and variants: a website's flags when a website is given, otherwise the organization-wide flags. Flag IDs are used by update_flag and add_users_to_flag.
new_text.list_funnels: List funnels for a website with their steps and filters. Funnel IDs are used by get_funnel_analytics.
new_text.list_github_repos: List GitHub repositories the organization's Databuddy GitHub App can read, with the website each is linked to. Use set_github_repo to link one.
new_text.list_goals: List conversion goals for a website with their type, target, and filters. Goal IDs are used by get_goal_analytics.
new_text.list_insights: List published insights for an organization or website: title, summary, evidence, impact, and the recorded next step (null when no step was recorded, when a later finding for the same case superseded it, or when the case resolved).
new_text.list_investigations: List the latest investigation per subject with IDs. state is needs_you, watching or resolved; need says what the team owes. Cases with dashboard work queued or running are left out until it finishes; get_investigation reads one by ID.
new_text.list_links: List short links for the website's organization, newest first, with every folder and its link count. create_link and update_link take those folder IDs or slugs and cannot create folders. search_links finds a specific link.
new_text.list_log_sources: List a website's linked backend logs, such as Axiom datasets, with one source's fields (name:type) and what they mean: fieldRoles (the field holding status, route, user_id...) and customerFields (fields matching people or accounts the website knows). Call before query_logs, whose filters use these n
new_text.list_profile_traits: List identified-user trait keys such as plan or role, with how many profiles have each and their top values. Use before filtering get_data by trait:<key> or search_replays by user traits.
new_text.list_replay_issues: List the last week's session replay friction: page elements whose clicks got no response (dead, rage or unresponsive clicks), most widespread first. Pass an issue key to search_replays issue to watch them.
new_text.list_slack_channels: List Slack channels in the organization's connected workspaces, marking the ones Databuddy posts investigations to. Use set_slack_channel to connect or remove one.
new_text.list_websites: List the websites this account can access, with IDs, names, domains, and organizations. Website-scoped tools accept websiteId, websiteName, or websiteDomain.
new_text.query_logs: Query a website's backend logs: filters, word search and aggregations (counts, percentiles, time series). Without aggregations it returns lines, newest first; repeat with cursor set to nextCursor for older ones. Count where failures are first, then read a few lines with fields set. Field names from
new_text.search_links: Find short links across the full catalog matching a substring on name, slug, target URL, or external ID, newest first.
new_text.search_replays: Find recordings by email, profileId, current user traits, recording dates, pages, timeline text, events, activity, or watch score. Use known trait values; ask if unknown. Dates refer to visits. Returns watch links, newest first.
new_text.set_github_repo: Link a website to its GitHub repository so its charts mark deploys and releases, unlink it with repository null, or choose which deployment environments and whether releases show. list_annotations' github lists the environments and current choice. Preview first; apply after the user approves.
new_text.set_slack_channel: Connect a Slack channel so Databuddy posts investigations and answers there, or remove it. Removing stops the posts; the app stays in the channel and a mention adds it back. Preview first; apply after the user approves.
new_text.submit_feedback: Send a bug report, feature request, or blocking error about Databuddy itself to the Databuddy team. Call only after the user asks or agrees to send it. Problems on the user's own website are analytics questions.
new_text.update_annotation: Update an annotation's text, tags, color, or visibility. Only annotations people added (source databuddy); GitHub markers are read-only. confirmed=false (default) returns the changes without writing; confirmed=true applies them.
new_text.update_flag: Change live flag evaluation settings. rules replaces all rules and needs expectedUpdatedAt. Preview returns current with full rules and updates; apply with confirmed=true after user approval.
new_text.update_funnel: Change a saved funnel's name, steps, filters, or conversion window for future analytics reads. Preview returns current and updates; apply only after user approval.
new_text.update_goal: Change a saved conversion goal used by future analytics reads. Preview returns current and updates; apply the reviewed changes only after user approval.
new_text.update_link: Change a saved short link, affecting subsequent redirects and social previews. Preview returns current, updates, and availableFolders; apply only after user approval.
new_text.update_log_fields: Correct which field of a linked log dataset holds a role, such as the customer's user ID, status code or route, or say no field does; later checks keep the choice. Or have Databuddy check the fields again. linkId and current roles from get_log_connection. Preview first; apply after the user approves
new_text.update_log_links: Link log datasets to websites so investigations and Databunny read them, or unlink them. Preview shows what each website would read; apply after the user approves. Adding a link a website already has replaces its scope.

Use it for a balloon mortgage or note whose payment is set on a long amort
new_text.debt_to_income: The debt-to-income ratio is total monthly debt payments divided by gross monthly income, shown as a percent, and this tool computes it for a borrower (plus the housing-only ratio, if given). Estimates, not offers or appraisals. CashForMyNote.com does not buy notes or make offers.
new_text.early_payoff_yield: When a note bought at a discount is paid off early, the discount is earned sooner and the yield rises, and this tool computes the yield if the borrower pays off after a chosen number of payments versus holding the note to maturity. Inputs are the price, balance, rate and payment terms you supply. Es
new_text.investment_to_value: Investment-to-value (ITV) is the price paid for a note, plus any senior liens, divided by the property's value, and this tool computes ITV beside the note's loan-to-value (LTV) and the value cushion behind the investment. It shows the collateral side of a mortgage note value calculation. Estimates,
new_text.land_contract_payoff: A land contract (contract for deed) payoff is the principal still owed plus interest accrued since the last payment, plus any other charges, and this tool computes that figure for a payoff date using a daily (per-diem) interest rate. Give the principal balance, or the original balance, payment and p
new_text.loan_payment: A fixed-rate loan's monthly payment is the level amount that pays off the balance with interest over the number of months, and this tool computes it for a mortgage, land contract or other installment note. new_text.loan_to_value: The loan-to-value ratio is the loan balance divided by the property's value, shown as a percent, and this tool computes LTV, combined LTV (CLTV) with other liens, and the equity cushion behind a note. Estimates, not offers or appraisals. CashForMyNote.com does not buy notes or make offers.
new_text.note_discount: A note's discount is how far its price is below the unpaid balance, and this tool gives it in dollars, as a percent, and in cents per dollar of balance. Estimates, not offers or appraisals. CashForMyNote.com does not buy notes or make offers.
new_text.note_price: A mortgage note's value is the present value of its remaining monthly payments (plus any balloon) at the yield a buyer requires, and this tool computes that price. It works the same for mortgage notes, land contracts (contracts for deed), owner-financed notes and other real estate notes. Optionally
new_text.note_yield: A note's yield is the annual return that makes its remaining payments (and any balloon) worth exactly the price paid, and this tool solves for it. It assumes every payment is made on time. Estimates, not offers or appraisals. CashForMyNote.com does not buy notes or make offers.
new_text.owner_financed_note: An owner-financed (seller-financed) note is the loan a seller carries for the buyer after the down payment, and this tool computes the note amount, monthly payment, loan-to-value at sale, any balloon, and the total of payments and interest. Use it to size a seller-carry note before you sell the prop
new_text.partial_purchase: In a partial note sale the holder sells only the next N payments and the rest revert to the holder, and this tool prices those payments at a target yield. new_text.prepayment_adjusted_value: Prepayments return principal early, which changes a note's value and shortens its life, and this tool prices a fully amortizing mortgage note at your target yield under a constant prepayment rate (CPR) you choose, beside its value with no prepayment and the weighted average life of each. Estimates,
new_text.remaining_balance: The remaining balance is the principal still owed after a number of on-time payments, and this tool computes it from the balance, rate and payment. Estimates, not offers or appraisals. CashForMyNote.com does not buy notes or make offers.
new_text.seasoning: A note's seasoning is how long the borrower has been paying, counted from the first payment due date, and this tool gives the months seasoned and the payments due so far. new_text.yield_ladder: A note's price falls as the yield a buyer requires rises, and this tool prices the same remaining payments at up to 12 yields side by side to show how much. Estimates, not offers or appraisals. CashForMyNote.com does not buy notes or make offers.

new_text.about_7maps: Call when asked what 7Maps is, or whether to use it. Returns what the map covers today, what each tool answers and a worked example. Not needed when you already know the tool you want. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp"}
new_text.changes_since: Call to check up to 50 servers you depend on at once. Returns only what changed since your date: outages, recoveries, tool changes, risk rises. Often nothing. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"servers":["https://mcp.example.com/mcp"],"since":"2026-11-20"}
new_text.claim_mcp_server: Call when the person owns a server on the map and wants it verified. First call returns proof options; call again with claim_check once the proof is in place. Never changes ranking. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp"}
new_text.find_tool: Call when you need a tool for a job and know no server. Returns matching tools with server address, estimated risk and whether the server answers now. Not for choosing among known servers (use route). Example: {"job":"send a transactional email","may":"read"}
new_text.list_paid_tools: Call before using a charged 7IT tool, to see how payment works and what the choices are. Returns the payment options and plan details. Not needed for the tools marked free. Example: {}
new_text.my_7maps_usage: Call when the person asks what 7Maps did for them. Returns their own counts for today, 7 days and 30 days, from the personal key sent with the connection. Without a key it says so. Example: {"window":"week"}
new_text.my_server_report: Call when the owner of a map server wants to see how agents looked for servers like theirs. Returns counts only, no agent identities. Read-only. Not for servers you do not own. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","days":30}
new_text.preflight: Call right before one planned tool call. Returns go, fix or no_go and what to change: server answers, tool exists, arguments fit. Does not call the server. new_text.report_road: Call after using a server to report how it went. Takes fixed fields only: worked or not, reason, time. Returns an acknowledgement. Not needed for a check-only question. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","tool":"create_booking","ok":false,"fail":"timeout"}
new_text.resolve: Call for a signed list of servers that answered at their last check. Returns up to 10 with a signature a client can verify. Never connects you. Not for a ranked pick (use route). Example: {"need":"send a transactional email","no_sign_in":true}
new_text.road_conditions: Call before using a server you have not used today. Returns up or down, sign-in need, speed, tool risk counts and last tool change. Reads the map; never calls the server. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp"}
new_text.route: Call when several servers could do a task and you want one pick. Returns the safest open server and tool, alternatives and servers to avoid. Not for searching tools (use find_tool). Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"task":"search company records","need":"read"}
new_text.submit_mcp_server: Call when a business has a server that is not listed and wants agents to find it. Returns a status page and an optional owner token. Observation takes days; listing is not guaranteed. Example: {"url":"example.com","category":"booking"}
new_text.tool_card: Call when you only need to pick a tool or prepare a call, not load a full tool list. Returns one compact card per tool: arguments, risk, side effects. Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","tools":["create_booking"]}
new_text.verify_lock: Call to check a server's tools against a lock you saved at approval. Returns per tool: unchanged, changed, removed or new, with any rise in risk. new_text.watch: Call before reusing a server a person approved earlier. Returns whether its tools changed since that date and whether the risk rose. Not for many servers (use changes_since). Charged tool: see list_paid_tools. Example: {"server":"https://mcp.example.com/mcp","approved_at":"2026-11-01"}

new_text.archive_coverage:
Anno per anno: pagine, fascicoli, testate, qualità media dell'OCR e anni senza pagine.

Per sapere se un periodo è coperto prima di trarre conclusioni da molti o pochi risultati.
new_text.explore_words:
Una parola nei giornali: grafie e frequenze, uso per decennio, famiglia, parole_vicine.

Le grafie sono le forme presenti (varianti d'epoca e storpiature dell'OCR); l'uso è per milione di parole
stampate; le parole_vicine sono quelle usate negli stessi contesti («nubifragio» per «alluvione»). Serve
new_text.fetch:
Rilegge il brano di un fonte_id (o di un id dei results di search): non la pagina intera (read_pages).

Un id cvp: indica la pagina corrente e ne legge i primi 6000 caratteri; per citare usare il fonte_id cv2
restituito, prossimo_inizio continua. Rifiuta se l'OCR o i metadati sono cambiati.
new_text.list_periodicals:
Le testate: sigla, anni e pagine conservate, genere, periodicità, collocazione. Gli anni sono quelli
conservati, non le date di vita della testata né una copertura continua.
new_text.read_pages:
Il testo OCR originale di pagine scelte; non cambia il conto dei piani. prossimo_inizio continua una
pagina lunga; un articolo può proseguire nella pagina dopo dello stesso fascicolo. Ogni pagina ha fonte_id.
new_text.read_passages:
I brani intorno ai riscontri di una query breve in pagine scelte, anche in fondo a pagine lunghe; al
massimo 48.000 caratteri. Restituisce fonte_id, termini trovati e mancanti, prossimo_brano. Non cambia il
conto dei piani.
new_text.research_continue:
Legge TUTTE le pagine del piano in ordine, a blocchi di circa 48.000 caratteri: solo per insiemi piccoli.

Fino a lettura_completa=true; le pagine consegnate sono contate lette e ripetere un cursore rilegge quel
blocco. Se blocco non è nullo, quella pagina resta da leggere.
new_text.research_discard:
Scarta pagine già mostrate nell'elenco con un motivo concreto, che resta nel conto; le pagine già lette
restano lette. Nel dubbio leggere.
new_text.research_list:
Continua l'ELENCO di un piano, circa 40.000 caratteri per volta; le righe già trattate portano [letta] o
[scartata], i numeri sono quelli dell'intero piano.
new_text.research_read:
Legge pagine dell'elenco, a strati (breve, contesto, integrale). Le pagine che non entrano tornano in
non_consegnate, una «parziale» riprende richiamandola. Ogni pagina ha fonte_id e url_fonte; segmenti[i] è il
fonte_id dell'estratto i. Il conto tiene la profondità più alta raggiunta.
new_text.research_start:
Ricerca CON CONTO: tutte le pagine delle piste, con l'ELENCO numerato (numero · fascicolo e pagina ·
piste · dove stanno le parole · riscontri · estratti OCR), panoramica e confronto_piste. Poi research_list
se continua, research_read, research_discard, research_status. Il piano restituito serve agl
new_text.research_status:
Il CONTO di una ricerca: lette (breve, contesto, integrali), scartate con i motivi, mancanti. Senza
ricevuta, nel processo locale, l'ultima ricerca.
new_text.search:
Occhiata veloce SENZA CONTO, con lo stesso motore del sito; per ricostruire usa research_start.
Con zero risultati la risposta dice quanto archivio c'era nel periodo.
new_text.search_many:
Occhiata veloce SENZA CONTO a più piste con filtri comuni: conteggi e prossimo_inizio per pista (non
sommare i totali), proposte_lettura per read_passages. Per una ricerca vera le stesse piste vanno in
research_start.
new_text.verify_quote:
Verifica una citazione nel brano di fonte_id: testo_originale, link preciso, riquadri. Nessuna lettera
corretta; la presenza del testo non prova l'interpretazione.
new_text.view_scan:
L'immagine della pagina originale dove l'OCR è dubbio in un punto che conta: quel punto con qualche riga
intorno e il suo testo OCR. Non per leggere pagine intere: il testo costa meno.
new_text.browse_issues:
I fascicoli usciti in un giorno, un mese o un anno, senza cercare parole: «cosa scrivevano i giornali il
4 novembre 1918?», i numeri di una testata in un anno, una citazione da ritrovare («Popolo Valtellinese, 12
gennaio 1924, p. 1»). Poi read_pages(fascicolo, pagina).

new_text.get_usage: This month's journey charges: by journey and model, against the team's monthly budget. Call this to see what the team's journeys have been charged this calendar month (UTC), and how much of its budget is left. (GET /api/usage)
new_text.list_domains: The team's domains: registration expiry, registrar, nameservers, status. Call this to check renewals. (GET /api/domains)
new_text.list_failed_checks: One site's failed checks: when, where, how, and whether each counted against uptime. Call this when uptime shows failures but no incident explains them. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/failures)
new_text.list_incidents: Incidents, open now or recent; open outages and slowdowns carry the likely cause. Call this to see what went wrong and why. (GET /api/incidents)
new_text.list_journey_runs: A journey's runs, newest first: verdicts, where they got stuck, costs and outcome checks. Call this to see how a journey has gone lately (the last 90 days) on one of its models, and to pick a run to read step by step. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/runs)
new_text.list_journeys: A site's agent journeys: what each asks an agent to do, its model and schedule, and its latest verdict. Call this to see how agents fare on the site. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys)
new_text.list_maintenance: One site's maintenance windows: on now, scheduled, and the last 30 days. Call this to see whether a site is in a maintenance window (its alerts held, its uptime not counting that time) and when the next one is. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/maintenance)
new_text.list_public_sites: Every public site's status and uptime, no key needed. Call this to see the public status pages' sites right now, without a key. (GET /api/public/sites)
new_text.list_scans: One site's API recovery scans, newest first: state, how each ended, and findings by weight. Call this to see whether a site has been scanned for dead ends, and how the last scan came out. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/scans)
new_text.list_site_events: What changed on one site: incidents opened and resolved, code pushes, maintenance, new pages. Call this to find what changed before a number moved (clicks fell, pages got slower). (GET /api/sites/{slug}/events)
new_text.list_sites: The team's sites: status, homepage uptime over 1, 7 and 30 days, open incidents. Call this to compare sites or report on uptime over the last day, week or month. (GET /api/sites)
new_text.pause_site: Pause a site's checks. Stops every check of the site, keeping its history, until it's resumed. Needs an Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/pause)
new_text.quote_journey: What the journey's next run would charge, on each of its models, and what's left to spend. Call this before running a journey now, or to tell your person what one costs. (GET /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/quote)
new_text.recheck_incident: Check an incident again now. The monitor checks it again within 30 seconds, after a fix, instead of waiting for the next scheduled check. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/incidents/{id}/recheck)
new_text.remeasure_site: Measure a site's headers and cache facts again now, after a fix. Call this after deploying a header or cache fix, instead of waiting for the daily run. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/insights/recheck)
new_text.renew_claim_link: A new claim link for your person. Makes a fresh claim link for an unclaimed site, from its results link's token, when you hand it over or your person lost theirs. Needs no key. (POST /start/s/{token}/claim)
new_text.resume_site: Resume a paused site's checks. Starts the site's checks again within a minute. Needs an Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/resume)
new_text.run_journey: Run a journey now, as a job. Queues a run on each of the journey's models, as Run now does. Needs an Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/journeys/{journey}/run)
new_text.start_maintenance: Start a maintenance window on a site now. Call this before a deploy. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/sites/{slug}/maintenance/start)
new_text.start_watching: Start watching a site, with no account, key or email. Starts checking a site's homepage now, for someone who has no account yet, and answers a private results link and a claim link for the person the agent works for. Needs no key. (POST /start)
new_text.undismiss_incident: Bring back a dismissed incident. Undoes a dismiss. Needs a Member or Admin key, on a team with 10 sites or more. (POST /api/incidents/{id}/undismiss)
